item.title: Implement ledger.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "Implement `ledger.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Context: repository root contains SPEC.md, ledger.py, test_ledger.py. Read SPEC.md in full first; it is the authority.

SPEC.md summary:
- Implement Ledger(balances), transfer(source, destination, amount) -> bool, snapshot() -> dict. MAX_BALANCE = 2**63 - 1 is the per-account ceiling.
- Construction: dict of nonempty string account names to built-in ints in [0, MAX_BALANCE]. Empty ledgers allowed. Invalid names, balances, or non-dict input raise ValueError. Booleans are not integers. Copy input; neither it nor returned snapshots may alias internal mutable state. Transfers cannot create accounts.
- Amount must be built-in int in [1, MAX_BALANCE], else ValueError. Validate amount before looking up accounts. Unknown source or destination raises KeyError.
- Return False for insufficient source funds or destination overflow; every failure leaves balances unchanged. Success returns True, debits and credits exactly the amount, preserves total.
- Transfer to the same account returns True iff the account has sufficient funds and never changes it (even at MAX_BALANCE); still validate amount and account first.
- All calls on one ledger are linearizable across threads: checks and both writes are one indivisible operation; snapshots never see a half transfer. Opposite transfers must not deadlock.
- Tests use no external services, no wall-clock calculations, no random inputs.

Requirements:
- Standard library only. Keep existing public API names and signatures.
- Keep functions under 60 lines, flat control flow, validation at boundaries, no swallowed exceptions, short comments only where non-obvious.
- Extend test_ledger.py (or keep it and add focused tests in the same file) covering: every ValueError case (bad names, bad balances incl. bool, bad amount incl. bool, non-dict), KeyError for unknown source/destination with amount validated first, insufficient funds, overflow at MAX_BALANCE, same-account transfers (sufficient, insufficient, at MAX_BALANCE), no-alias on construction and snapshot, failure leaves state unchanged, total preserved, and a deterministic multi-thread test including opposite transfers that must not deadlock (use a fixed thread count and fixed operations, no randomness, no timing thresholds).
- Run the tests with the standard library (python -m unittest or pytest if already used) and make sure they pass before committing.
- Commit the work in this repository with the existing git identity. Do not override git identity. Do not add any attribution line claiming Claude or AI authorship. Do not push.

pr.body: Approach: Ledger stores validated copies of balances. Module helpers _check_account_name, _check_balance and _check_amount enforce built-in int (bool rejected) and range rules at the boundary. transfer validates the amount, then under one threading.Lock checks both accounts exist (KeyError), handles same-account transfers without writes, returns False on insufficient funds or destination overflow, and otherwise writes both sides. snapshot copies under the same lock. Key files: ledger.py, test_ledger.py. Checks: python3 -B -m unittest -v, 27 tests OK. Assumptions: a single per-ledger lock is sufficient for linearizability and deadlock freedom; account names must be exact str; non-str account lookups raise KeyError. Follow-ups (non-blocking): worker exceptions are not propagated by run_threads; the split-lock mutant is only probabilistically caught; no overdraft race test; sequential joins mean a deadlock reports after up to 30 s per thread.
pr.summary: Made the atomic Ledger real. Now: transfers validate, check and write under one lock; snapshots never see a half transfer. Before: stubs raising NotImplementedError. Now: full spec API plus 27 tests covering every error and boundary case and deterministic thread runs.
pr.title: Implement Ledger per SPEC.md with focused tests

risk.why: Concurrency and locking: a single lock is the only guard for atomic check-and-write and snapshot consistency. Touches ledger.py and test_ledger.py only, with no callers outside this repo. Behaviour is new (stubs replaced). Reviewer 3 confirmed risk high; reviewers flagged the concurrency tests as probabilistic.
